text:
⛽ Official: petrol barely moves on Wednesday 4 November. Petrol 93 and 95 drop just 1 cent a litre, so inland 95 stays at about R30.24. Diesel falls R1.10 (0.05%) to R1.20 (0.005%) a litre. But paraffin goes up R2.75 a litre (wholesale) and LPG gas R1.83 a kg (R2.08 in the Western Cape), which hits households that cook with them.

Without the fuel levy cut from the Medium-Term Budget, petrol would have risen about R1.49 a litre and diesel about R1.80 to R1.90. Oil averaged $108 a barrel (up from $101), the rand weakened to R16.55 a dollar, and the slate levy jumped 48c to R1.36 a litre to recover a R15.9 billion shortfall. The relief runs until 1 December, then shrinks until 5 January.

Without-cut figures calculated: petrol -1+150=+149c; diesel 300-109.82=+190c, 300-119.82=+180c. Inland 95 Oct R30.25 (oilprices.co.za/DMPR) -1c = R30.24. CHECK: zone price schedule published 3 Nov.
